propositions: A flat per-context character bound (_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS=100,000) conflates physical model-window capacity with economic per-criterion fan-out cost, causing legitimate contexts to be refused at preflight when the product context_chars × criteria_count remains under the ratified worst case

The live c9f7 context (121,147 chars × 22 criteria = 2.67M product) is refused by recovery preflight because context alone exceeds 100,000, even though the product is under the previously approved 3.2M ceiling (32 criteria × 100k)

The physical ceiling must be derived from the resolved verifier model's own context window (not escalation max), and the economic ceiling must be expressed as a product bound to allocate headroom where real tickets need it

The two-ceiling approach (physical: window-derived × 2 chars/token conservative factor; economic: 3.2M char-product interim bound) unblocks c9f7 re-certification while preserving the invariant that no context is elided and over-budget refusals make zero billable calls
